cards.title: Capital Influx
cards.description: A historic week driven by Neysa AI's unicorn round and aggressive deeptech funding across the ecosystem.

cards.title: Infra Pledge
cards.description: Massive private commitments from Adani and AM Group to build green, renewable-powered AI data centres by 2035.

cards.title: Global Talent
cards.description: A new whitepaper reveals India now houses nearly one-fifth of the world's total AI workforce, solidifying its talent dominance.

cards.title: Sovereign Models
cards.description: Sarvam AI and BharatGen debuted as India's first indigenous foundational models, reducing reliance on foreign tech stacks.

cards.title: Compute Sovereignty
cards.description: India is aggressively pivoting from an AI consumer to a creator. With the launch of indigenous foundational models like Sarvam and BharatGen, coupled with the government's push for a "sovereign compute" stack, the nation is building the hardware and software backbone necessary to secure strategic autonomy in the AI era.

cards.title: The 'Third Way' Doctrine
cards.description: The India AI Impact Summit highlighted a geopolitical alignment between India and France, pitching a "Third Way" that avoids total dependence on US or Chinese models. Through the "MANAV" vision and the 7-Sutra framework, India is positioning itself as the leader for responsible, human-centric AI governance for the Global South.

cards.title: Algorithmic Enforcement
cards.description: AI has moved from back-office efficiency to frontline enforcement. The discovery of a ₹70,000 crore tax evasion scam using advanced data analytics signals a new era of algorithmic governance. Simultaneously, corporate India is restructuring to meet this reality, with a reported surge in "Chief AI Officer" hirings across enterprise sectors.

cards.title: The Deeptech Renaissance
cards.description: The unicorn drought has ended with Neysa AI's massive $1.2Bn valuation, signalling renewed investor confidence in India's deeptech capabilities. Validating this shift, global giants like Qualcomm ($150M fund) and Google (undersea cables) are moving beyond service contracts to invest directly in India's IP creation and infrastructure.
